verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna sorts knowledge, action, doers, judgement, resolve and happiness by the three qualities.
verse.sanskrit: मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः । सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.
verse.translation: The doer who is free from attachment, does not speak of himself, is full of steadiness and enthusiasm, and unmoved by success or failure, is called sattvic.
verse.why: Choose the joy that's hard at first and sweet later.

verse.meaning: Krishna is sorting out what makes a good action and a good doer. He speaks to Arjuna, who is standing at the edge of a great battle, unsure of how to act. verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on working in the world without being stained by it.
verse.sanskrit: युक्तः कर्मफलं त्यक्त्वा शान्तिमाप्नोति नैष्ठिकीम् । अयुक्तः कामकारेण फले सक्तो निबध्यते ॥
verse.line: Let go of the payoff and you find lasting peace. Chase it and it chains you.
verse.translation: The disciplined person, giving up the fruit of action, attains lasting peace. The undisciplined, attached to the fruit and driven by desire, is bound.
verse.why: Be in the mess without letting it soak in.
verse.misuse: Letting go of the payoff isn't refusing fair pay or recognition; it's not being chained to it.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna, who stands paralyzed by doubt on the edge of a battle he does not want to fight. verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.sanskrit: ऐहिकः प्राक्तनं हन्ति प्राक्तनोऽद्यतनं बलात् । सर्वदा पुरुषस्पन्दस्तत्रानुद्वेगवाञ्जयी ॥
verse.line: Today's effort and yesterday's keep wrestling. Whoever stays calm through it wins.
verse.translation: Present effort overcomes the past, and the past can overpower the present. It is always a contest of human striving, and the one who stays calm wins.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha is speaking to the young Rama, who is feeling lost after losing his kingdom. He tells him that what people call fate is nothing but the result of past effort, and that present effort can overcome it. The stronger of two rams wins, and the one who stays calm through the contest of striving is the one who wins. Do not grieve over what was never in your hands.
verse.for_you: You want to stay consistent through the hard year ahead, but the highs and lows are already here. Your past effort shaped today. Today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands. Whoever stays calm through it wins.

verse.setting: The monkeys searching for Sita are exhausted and failing; young Angada rallies them.

verse.line: Keep working and the results will come. Sink into despair and it is hard to get back up.

story.title: Building the bridge
story.story_hook: The army stood on the shore with no boats, until a quiet monkey said he knew how to build a bridge.
story.summary: Ram waits three days for the ocean to let him pass, then loses patience. The ocean reveals that Nala can build a bridge; Nala admits his skill and the whole army hauls trees and rocks for five days until the bridge reaches Lanka.
story.lesson: Big things get built by many hands, once someone admits they know how.

script: You signed your first paying customer yesterday. After fourteen months, there it is. You know the hard part starts now. You want to stay grounded through the year ahead, and you are anxious about how things will turn out. That mix is real.
Arjuna is standing at the edge of a great battle, unsure of how to act. He is trembling with grief and doubt. And Krishna replies:
मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहंवादी धृत्युत्साहसमन्वितः, सिद्ध्यसिद्ध्योर्निर्विकारः कर्ता सात्त्विक उच्यते.
In plain words: Free of clinging and boasting, full of resolve and enthusiasm, unchanged by success or failure: the best kind of doer.

Krishna is sorting out what makes a good action and a good doer. The best kind of person acts without holding on to the result. They do not boast about what they are doing. They stay steady whether things go well or not. This is the kind of action that brings true clarity. This is easier said than done, because every instinct pulls you toward the result. You want to hold on to the win, but the work itself is what will carry you. The joy here is poison first and nectar later.
Let that first customer land without letting it define your next step. Stay steady in the doing, not in the reward. The milestone is real, but it is only the start of the practice.
What will you do today before the result arrives?
